title: Sparse cyclic Weyl operators in prime-power dimension: an operator extension of the scalar uncertainty law through sparsity $2p-1$
abstract: Let $d=p^k$ and let $W_{(a,b)}=X^aZ^b$ be the cyclic Weyl operators on $\mathbb C^d$. Write $w_p(r)$ for the base-$p$ digit weight $\prod_t(r_t+1)$ and $\Omega_k(m)=\max\{r<p^k:w_p(r)\le m\}$. We give a valuation proof of the classical Delvaux–Van Barel scalar law: (Z) a polynomial with at most $m$ terms and degree below $d$ annihilates at most $\Omega_k(m)$ of the $d$-th roots of unity, and this is sharp. Our operator extension is: (B) every nonzero combination $C$ of $\ell\le2p-1$ Weyl operators satisfies $\dim\ker C\le\Omega_k(\ell)$, i.e. $\operatorname{rank}C\ge p^k-(\ell-1)p^{k-1}$ for $\ell\le p$ (sharp) and $\operatorname{rank}C\ge p^{k-1}$ for $p\le\ell\le2p-1$. The commutative ingredient is the Massey–Costello–Justesen weight-retaining property; the operator ingredient is a Radon-type lemma showing that first-order obstructions have weight at least $2p$. For composite $d$ the maximal nullity is $d/p_{\min}$ at sparsity two and, conditionally on a published trinomial rank rule, $\max(2d/r_3,\,d/2\,[d\text{ even}])$ at sparsity three. The conjecture $\dim\ker C\le\Omega_k(s_W(C))$ for all sparsities is proved for $d\in\{4,8,9\}$ and for torsion cosets; its first open case is $d=16$, $\ell=6$.
